scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

So, the person took most of the stuff to the dump but kept the video games and sold them for $600. Now, legally, it seems like there's nothing wrong with what the person did because the roommate didn't respond to the attempts to contact him. But the roommate is upset and calling the person an asshole, asking for the money back. So, is it right or wrong? I think it depends on the perspective. From the person's side, they were trying to be responsible by contacting the roommate and avoiding the expensive removal fees. Selling the games was a way to recover some of the costs or maybe even make a bit of money. But from the roommate's side, it's about ownership. The games were his, and selling them without his consent feels like theft, even if the person tried to contact him. I also wonder about the intent. Did the person sell the games to make money, or was it to avoid the landlord's fees? If it was the latter, maybe it's more justifiable. But if it was to profit, that might be seen as wrong. Another angle is the relationship between the two. They were roommates, and now there's tension. The person handled the situation by selling the games, which led to conflict. Maybe there's a better way to handle it, like donating the games or finding another solution that doesn't involve selling them. Also, the roommate left without paying the last rent, which might make the person feel justified in taking action. But does that give the person the right to sell the roommate's belongings? Legally, maybe not, but morally, it's a gray area. I'm also thinking about the value of the games. $600 is a significant amount. If the roommate had wanted to keep the games, that's a lot of money lost. But if the games were just taking up space and the roommate didn't care, then maybe it's not as bad. In the end, it's a tough call. The person did what they thought was necessary to handle the situation, but it hurt the roommate. Maybe the best approach would have been to find a way to return the games or handle the situation without selling them, even if it meant more hassle or cost. So, I'm leaning towards it being somewhat wrong because it involved selling someone else's property without their consent, even if there were good reasons. But I can understand why the person did it, given the circumstances.
